description: Extract the three inline list components (DetailList, CardGridList, CompactList) into a single PlaceCard component that adapts via a cardLayout prop
steps: Create components/near-me/place-card.tsx with a PlaceCard component that accepts: place, index, cardLayout ('grid' | 'list' | 'compact'), topic, selected, hovered, saved, onSelect, onHoverPlace, onToggleSave
Move all list rendering out of near-me-view.tsx into PlaceCard; near-me-view.tsx should only map over places and render <PlaceCard> per item inside a wrapper div
The 'grid' cardLayout is a vertical card (photo on top, info below) — used by food-eating and social-belonging
The 'list' cardLayout is a horizontal card (photo left, info right, action column right) — used by health-wellbeing and home-admin
The 'compact' cardLayout is a slim row with a transit icon circle instead of a photo — used only by getting-around
Derive cardLayout from topicMeta.layout: 'card-grid' → 'grid', 'list-focus' → 'list', 'map-focus' → 'compact' (except getting-around which stays compact and social-belonging which switches to 'grid')
Verify all 5 topic tabs render the correct layout after the extraction
Verify selected/hover border highlight and row scroll-into-view still work correctly

description: All cards lead with a photo — hero image for grid cards, thumbnail for list cards, transit icon for compact rows
steps: In PlaceCard grid layout: render a full-width hero image at h-44 using object-cover; overlay the place number badge (bottom-left, dark pill) and heart button (top-right) directly on the photo

In PlaceCard list layout: render an 80×80 rounded-lg thumbnail on the left; if no thumbnail, render a square tile with the topic icon centered on a topic-tinted background (food: amber/10, health: green/10, home: teal/10)
In PlaceCard compact layout: render a 40×40 circle with the transit mode emoji centered on bg-blue-100; do not show a photo at all for getting-around
For grid and list layouts, when place.thumbnail is absent, show a gray fog tile with a centered MapPin icon (size-6 text-minuri-silver)
Verify hero photos load with Next.js Image fill + sizes='(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 50vw'
Verify the number overlay badge is visible against both light and dark photos (dark semi-transparent background)

description: Yelp-style rating row: yellow star + rating number + review count in muted text, replacing the dark pill badge
steps: Define a RatingRow component: renders ⭐ (yellow star emoji) + rating in font-semibold text-sm + '(' + reviewCount formatted with k suffix + ')' in text-xs text-minuri-slate/70
Format review count: >= 1000 → '{n}k' (e.g. '1.2k'), < 1000 → exact number
Replace all existing dark bg-minuri-mid rating pill badges with RatingRow across PlaceCard grid, list, and popup card in near-me-map.tsx
Suppress RatingRow for topic === 'social-belonging' (belonging is not ranked)
Verify RatingRow renders inline with the place name in grid cards and in its own line under the name in list cards
Verify no rating badge appears on any social-belonging card

description: Open/closed status shows specific closing or next-open time parsed from open_state for all topics, not just health-wellbeing
steps: In lib/near-me.ts, add a parseOpenState(raw: string | undefined): { isOpen: boolean; label: string } helper that extracts the time substring: 'Open ⋅ Closes 10 pm' → { isOpen: true, label: 'until 10 pm' }, 'Closed ⋅ Opens Mon 8 am' → { isOpen: false, label: 'opens Mon 8 am' }, fallback to { isOpen: /open/i.test(raw), label: '' }
In PlaceCard, render an OpenBadge using parseOpenState(place.hours): when isOpen → green dot + 'Open' + label in text-green-700; when closed → red dot + 'Closed' + label in text-red-600

Display the OpenBadge on all topic cards: in grid layout it sits below the place name on its own line; in list layout it appears in the right-hand status column; in compact layout it is omitted (transit stops have no meaningful open hours)
Remove the topic === 'health-wellbeing' condition that previously gated the open/closed badge
Verify 'Open until 10 pm' renders in green on an open food-eating card
Verify 'Closed · opens Mon 8 am' renders in red on a closed health-wellbeing card

description: Price range displayed inline next to type as a single muted meta row, not as a separate tag chip
steps: In PlaceCard, compose a single meta line: '{type} · {price} · {distance}' where each segment is omitted when absent
Style: text-xs text-minuri-slate/80; price portion shown as text-minuri-slate font-medium ($ $$ $$$ stand out slightly)
Remove price from the tags/chips rendering — price is no longer displayed as a chip
Retain service_options chips (Dine-in, Takeaway, Delivery) separately below the meta line for food-eating topic only
Verify the meta line reads e.g. 'Restaurant · $$ · 1.2 km' on a food-eating card with location active
Verify the meta line reads e.g. 'GP clinic · 0.5 km' on a health-wellbeing card (no price shown)

description: Distance shown as a '📍 0.8 km' pill badge near the address when user location is active
steps: Remove distanceKm from the inline address text ('123 Main St · 0.8 km')
Instead render a separate pill badge: '📍 0.8 km' with bg-green-50 text-green-700 text-[10px] rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 positioned to the right of the address line
Only render the badge when place.distanceKm is defined (location active)
In compact layout, show distanceKm as plain text to the right of the stop name (no pill — space is too tight)
Verify the distance badge appears when usingLocation is true and disappears otherwise

description: Unified action strip at the bottom of every PlaceCard with a topic-aware primary CTA and consistent secondary buttons
steps: Define a unified action row for PlaceCard with: primary button (rounded-full, bg-minuri-teal text-white, full-width on mobile), then secondary buttons (outlined rounded-full, border-minuri-silver/60)

Primary CTA per topic: food-eating → '↗ Directions'; getting-around (public-transit subtype) → 'Plan journey'; getting-around (cycling) → '↗ Directions'; health-wellbeing → '📞 Call to book' (when phone exists) or '↗ Directions'; home-admin → '🌐 Visit website' (when website exists) or '↗ Directions'; social-belonging → '↗ Directions'
Secondary buttons: phone button when topic is not getting-around and place.phone exists; website button when topic is home-admin and both phone and website exist; all buttons use e.stopPropagation()
Heart button (HeartButton component) moves into the photo overlay (top-right corner) for grid cards; stays in the action row for list and compact cards
Verify primary CTA fills full width on mobile; secondary buttons wrap below on small screens
Verify Call button opens tel: link and Directions opens Google Maps in a new tab without navigating away from Near Me

description: Food & Eating tab renders a 2-column card grid on desktop (1 column on mobile) with photo-dominant cards
steps: In near-me-view.tsx, the results wrapper for topic === 'food-eating' renders: <div className='grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-0 divide-y divide-minuri-silver/30 md:divide-y-0 md:gap-3 md:p-3'>

Each PlaceCard in grid layout shows: hero photo h-44, number badge overlay bottom-left, heart overlay top-right, then below: name (font-semibold text-base), RatingRow, meta line (type · price · distance), OpenBadge, service_options chips (up to 3), snippet (2 lines max, italic text-xs), action row [Directions] + [Call]
Service option chips use bg-amber-50 text-amber-700 text-[10px] rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 to distinguish from the teal subtype chips
Snippet is capped at 2 lines using line-clamp-2 to keep cards uniform height
Verify cards render in 2 columns on desktop and stack to 1 column on mobile
Verify heart overlay is clickable independently of the card click (stopPropagation)

description: Getting Around tab renders slim transit rows with a transit mode icon circle, no photo hero
steps: In near-me-view.tsx, the results wrapper for topic === 'getting-around' renders: <div className='divide-y divide-minuri-silver/30'>

Each compact PlaceCard shows: [40×40 circle with transit emoji centered on bg-blue-100] [main content: stop name (font-medium text-sm), short address (first segment), distance badge] [right: Plan journey button or Directions]
The transit emoji in the circle is derived from getTransitBadge(place.type): 🚂 Train / 🚊 Tram / 🚌 Bus / 🚲 Bike / 🗺 Transit
The action button for public-transit subtype links to https://www.ptv.vic.gov.au/journey in a new tab; for cycling subtype it links to Google Maps Directions
Do not render a snippet, tags, or service options for getting-around — keep rows minimal so the map takes visual priority
Verify the list panel stays narrow (map-focus width) and the map fills the right two-thirds

description: Health & Wellbeing tab renders a 3-zone horizontal list card: photo | info | status+CTA column
steps: In near-me-view.tsx, the results wrapper for topic === 'health-wellbeing' renders: <div className='divide-y divide-minuri-silver/30'>

Each list PlaceCard shows three horizontal zones in a flex row: left (80×80 thumbnail or green-tinted icon tile), center (flex-1: name bold, type + bulk-billing nudge tag, address + distance, snippet 1 line italic), right (shrink-0 w-28: OpenBadge stacked above primary CTA)
Right column primary CTA: '📞 Call to book' button (full-width, teal fill) when place.phone exists; '↗ Directions' otherwise
Bulk-billing nudge renders as a small amber tag (bg-amber-50 text-amber-700 border border-amber-200 text-[10px]) directly below the type text, only for health-wellbeing topic
A secondary action row spans full card width at the bottom: [Directions] outlined + [Website] outlined — only rendered if phone was used as primary CTA
Verify the 3-zone layout does not overflow on mobile — collapse to 2-zone (no right column) on screens < 640px, stacking the OpenBadge and CTA below the center info

description: Home & Admin tab renders a single-column list with website as the primary prominent action
steps: In near-me-view.tsx, the results wrapper for topic === 'home-admin' renders: <div className='divide-y divide-minuri-silver/30'>
Each list PlaceCard shows: [80×80 thumbnail OR icon tile — 📋 for services subtype / 📚 for libraries subtype on bg-teal-50] [center: name, type, address + distance, snippet] [no right column]

Below the center info, render a dedicated action row that spans full width: '🌐 Visit website' as a full-width teal-fill button (when place.website exists), then '↗ Directions' as a full-width outlined button below it
When no website is available, '↗ Directions' becomes the full-width primary button
Phone button rendered as a small inline link (not a full button) below the website button when place.phone exists
Verify the website button is the most visually prominent element for home-admin cards
Verify the icon tile (📋 or 📚) renders correctly when no SerpAPI thumbnail is returned for government services

description: Social & Belonging tab renders a 2-column discovery grid matching food-eating grid but without rating
steps: In near-me-view.tsx, the results wrapper for topic === 'social-belonging' renders: <div className='grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-0 divide-y divide-minuri-silver/30 md:divide-y-0 md:gap-3 md:p-3'>

Each grid PlaceCard shows: hero photo h-44, heart overlay top-right (no number badge for social-belonging — discovery mode feels less ranked), then: name (font-semibold), meta line (type · price · distance, no rating), OpenBadge
community-spaces subtype: render '📅 Check venue for events' amber chip below the meta line
social-venues subtype: render price level chips ($ $$ $$$) from place.tags in teal/10 below the meta line
Action row: [↗ Directions] outlined as the sole action (community events are about going there, not calling)
Verify no rating appears on any social-belonging card
Verify the discovery grid feel — no numbered badges, discovery-first photo emphasis

description: Add parseOpenState() helper that extracts closing/opening time from the open_state string for Yelp-style status display
steps: In lib/near-me.ts, add: export function parseOpenState(raw: string | undefined): { isOpen: boolean; label: string }

Parse patterns: 'Open ⋅ Closes 10 pm' → { isOpen: true, label: 'until 10 pm' }; 'Closed ⋅ Opens Mon 8 am' → { isOpen: false, label: 'opens Mon 8 am' }; 'Open 24 hours' → { isOpen: true, label: '24 hours' }
When raw is undefined or empty return { isOpen: false, label: '' }
When no time pattern is found, fall back to isOpen: /open/i.test(raw) and label: ''
Use parseOpenState everywhere the open/closed status is rendered — PlaceCard and near-me-map.tsx popup
Verify 'until 10 pm' appears in the open badge when SerpAPI returns 'Open ⋅ Closes 10 pm'

description: Add photos?: string[] to NearMePlace and map from API response for a photo strip on list-layout cards
steps: In lib/near-me.ts, add photos?: string[] to the NearMePlace type
In near-me-view.tsx fetchPlaces(), map place.photos (once backend sends it) to NearMePlace.photos — slice to 3 max

In PlaceCard list layout (health-wellbeing, home-admin), when place.photos has 2 or more entries, render a horizontal strip of h-14 w-20 rounded thumbnails below the center info zone and above the action row
Use Next.js Image with fill in a relative container; strip scrolls horizontally on overflow
Fallback gracefully — when photos is empty or undefined, render nothing; do not leave an empty strip container
Verify photo strip appears on a health-wellbeing card that has multiple SerpAPI photos

description: [BACKEND FIX REQUIRED] Add phone, website, service_options, and photos to NearbyInterestItemResponse and extract them in _normalize_place()
steps: In app/schemas/near_me.py, add to NearbyInterestItemResponse: phone: str | None = None, website: str | None = None, service_options: list[str] | None = None, photos: list[str] | None = None

In app/services/near_me.py _normalize_place(), add to the returned dict: 'phone': place.get('phone'), 'website': place.get('website'), 'service_options': place.get('service_options'), and photos logic below
For photos: collect [place.get('thumbnail')] + [img.get('thumbnail') or img.get('original') for img in place.get('photos', [])]; filter None values; deduplicate; slice to first 3
Verify that a test call to search_near_me(suburb='Richmond', topic='food-eating', subtype='food-dining') returns results with phone and website populated for most places
Verify service_options returns a list like ['Dine-in', 'Takeaway', 'Delivery'] for restaurants
Verify photos returns a list of at most 3 URLs (thumbnail counted as first photo)

description: [BACKEND FIX REQUIRED] Switch SerpAPI engine from 'google' to 'google_maps' for local_results with richer fields including hours, phone, and website
steps: In app/services/near_me.py search_near_me(), change the engine parameter from 'google' to 'google_maps'
For google_maps engine, update the search params: replace 'q' with 'q', keep 'location', add 'type': 'search'; remove 'gl', 'google_domain', 'hl' (google_maps uses different params)
The google_maps engine returns local_results as a list directly (not nested under 'places'); verify _extract_places() handles both formats — it currently does
Google Maps results include: 'phone', 'website', 'hours' (as a list of day objects), 'service_options', 'thumbnail', 'photos' — verify extraction in _normalize_place()
For hours extraction: the google_maps engine returns hours as a list [{'day': 'Monday', 'hours': '8 am–10 pm'}, ...]; flatten to a single open_state string from the current day or the first day
Verify the switch does not break the suburb + query search pattern
NOTE: If google_maps engine returns fewer results than 'google', consider falling back to 'google' for topics where map coverage is thin (getting-around)
